1→# Common Houdini Geometry Attributes
     2→
     3→## Point Attributes
     4→| Attribute | Type | Description |
     5→|-----------|------|-------------|
     6→| `P` | vector3 | Position (x, y, z) |
     7→| `N` | vector3 | Normal vector |
     8→| `Cd` | vector3 | Color (r, g, b) in 0-1 range |
     9→| `Alpha` | float | Opacity (0=transparent, 1=opaque) |
    10→| `v` | vector3 | Velocity (units/second) |
    11→| `w` | vector4 | Angular velocity (quaternion) |
    12→| `orient` | vector4 | Orientation quaternion |
    13→| `pscale` | float | Point scale (uniform) |
    14→| `scale` | vector3 | Non-uniform scale |
    15→| `up` | vector3 | Up vector (for copy-to-points) |
    16→| `id` | int | Stable particle ID (survives death/birth) |
    17→| `age` | float | Particle age in seconds |
    18→| `life` | float | Particle lifespan in seconds |
    19→| `rest` | vector3 | Rest position (for texturing deforming geo) |
    20→| `uv` | vector3 | UV texture coordinates |
    21→| `shop_materialpath` | string | Material assignment path |
    22→
    23→## Primitive Attributes
    24→| Attribute | Type | Description |
    25→|-----------|------|-------------|
    26→| `name` | string | Prim group name (used by Solaris for USD paths) |
    27→| `shop_materialpath` | string | Per-prim material assignment |
    28→| `path` | string | USD/Alembic hierarchy path |
    29→
    30→## Detail Attributes
    31→| Attribute | Type | Description |
    32→|-----------|------|-------------|
    33→| `varmap` | string | Variable mapping for shaders |
    34→
    35→## Vertex Attributes
    36→| Attribute | Type | Description |
    37→|-----------|------|-------------|
    38→| `uv` | vector3 | Per-vertex UV (overrides point UV) |
    39→| `N` | vector3 | Per-vertex normal (overrides point normal) |
    40→| `Cd` | vector3 | Per-vertex color |
    41→
    42→## Special Attributes for Copy-to-Points
    43→The `copytopoints` SOP reads these from target points:
    44→- `P` - Position (required)
    45→- `orient` - Quaternion rotation (highest priority)
    46→- `N` + `up` - Rotation from normal+up (if no orient)
    47→- `pscale` - Uniform scale
    48→- `scale` - Non-uniform scale (vector3)
    49→- `v` - Velocity (for motion blur)
    50→
    51→## Pyro/Volume Attributes
    52→| Attribute | Type | Description |
    53→|-----------|------|-------------|
    54→| `density` | float | Smoke/fire density (0-1+) |
    55→| `temperature` | float | Heat for buoyancy |
    56→| `flame` | float | Visible flame (0-1) |
    57→| `fuel` | float | Combustible fuel |
    58→| `vel` | vector3 | Volume velocity field |
    59→
    60→## FLIP Fluid Attributes
    61→| Attribute | Type | Description |
    62→|-----------|------|-------------|
    63→| `viscosity` | float | Per-particle viscosity override |
    64→| `surface` | float | Surface distance (from particlefluidsurface) |
    65→| `vorticity` | vector3 | Curl of velocity field |
    66→| `droplet` | float | Isolated particle flag (for spray meshing) |
    67→
    68→## Constraints (RBD)
    69→| Attribute | Type | Description |
    70→|-----------|------|-------------|
    71→| `constraint_name` | string | Constraint type identifier |
    72→| `constraint_type` | int | 0=position, 1=rotation |
    73→| `strength` | float | Breaking threshold |
    74→| `anchor_name` | string | Connected piece name |
    75→
    76→## Intrinsic Attributes (read via primintrinsic())
    77→| Attribute | Description |
    78→|-----------|-------------|
    79→| `measuredarea` | Surface area of prim |
    80→| `measuredperimeter` | Perimeter of prim |
    81→| `measuredvolume` | Volume of closed mesh |
    82→| `typename` | Prim type ("Poly", "BezierCurve", etc.) |
    83→| `packedfulltransform` | Full transform of packed prim |

content.content:
1→# Joy of VEX: Color
     2→
     3→> Tutorial examples from The Joy of VEX video series by Matt Estela.
     4→> Source: https://www.youtube.com/@MattEstela
     5→
     6→## Quick Reference
     7→```vex
     8→@Cd = @N.y;  // Vector Component Access
     9→@Cd = @P.x + 3;  // Offsetting Color Values
    10→@Cd = @P;  // Position to Color Mapping
    11→```
    12→
    13→## Color Operations
    14→
    15→### Distance-Based Color with Sine Wave [[Ep1, 109:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=6554s)]
    16→```vex
    17→vector pos = @P * chv('fancyscale');
    18→vector center = chv('center');
    19→float d = distance(pos, center);
    20→d *= ch('scalePos');
    21→@Cd = fit(sin(d*chf('time')),-1,1,0,1);
    22→```
    23→Creates an animated color pattern by calculating the distance from each point to a center position, applying a sine wave modulated by time, and fitting the result to color values. The position is first scaled by a vector channel parameter, and the distance is further scaled before the sine function creates oscillating values that are remapped from [-1,1] to [0,1] for color output.
    24→
    25→## Color from Normals
    26→
    27→### Vectors as Color Components [[Ep1, 14:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=866s)]
    28→```vex
    29→@Cd = @P;
    30→
    31→@Cd = @N;
    32→
    33→@Cd = @P.x;
    34→```
    35→Demonstrates how vectors can be assigned to color attributes since both are three-component values. The normal vector @N (0,1,0 for upward-pointing normals) maps directly to RGB color space, resulting in green when all normals point up. On curved geometry like a sphere or pig head, varying normal directions produce different colors based on their directional components.
    36→
    37→### Visualizing normals with color [Needs Review] [[Ep1, 14:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=896s)]
    38→```vex
    39→@Cd = @P;
    40→
    41→@Cd = @N;
    42→
    43→@Cd = @N.x;
    44→```
    45→Demonstrates how position (@P) and normal (@N) vectors can be visualized as RGB colors by assigning them to @Cd. When normals are assigned to color, the resulting RGB values create a visual representation similar to normal maps, with different colors indicating different vector directions. Individual components (like @N.x) can also be visualized, showing a single color channel.
    46→
    47→## Color from Position
    48→
    49→### Position to Color Mapping [[Ep1, 15:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=900s)]
    50→```vex
    51→@Cd = @P;
    52→
    53→@Cd = @P.x;
    54→```
    55→Demonstrates mapping position (@P) directly to color (@Cd), which visualizes spatial coordinates as RGB values. The first example maps the full vector to color, while the second extracts only the X component, creating a gradient. This technique produces colors similar to normal maps, where position/direction values translate to visible color variations across the geometry.
    56→
    57→## Color from Normals
    58→
    59→### Mapping Attributes to Color [[Ep1, 15:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=940s)]
    60→```vex
    61→@Cd = @N;
    62→
    63→@Cd = @P;
    64→
    65→@Cd = @P.x;
    66→```
    67→Demonstrates assigning different point attributes to color (@Cd). Setting @Cd = @N creates normal-map-like colors with bluish-greenish-reddish hues based on surface orientation. Setting @Cd = @P uses world-space position values as color, which can result in negative values (over-saturated or under-saturated colors outside the 0-1 range).
    68→
    69→## Color from Position
    70→
    71→### Assigning Position to Color [[Ep1, 16:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=960s)]
    72→```vex
    73→@Cd = @P;
    74→
    75→@Cd = @P;
    76→
    77→@Cd = @P.x;
    78→```
    79→Demonstrates assigning position values directly to color attributes. Setting @Cd to @P maps XYZ position values to RGB color channels, creating a spatial color gradient. Accessing individual components like @P.x allows isolating specific position axes for color assignment, though this can produce invalid color values when positions are negative or out of the 0-1 range.
    80→
    81→## Color from Normals
    82→
    83→### Position to Color Mapping Components [[Ep1, 17:00](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=1020s)]
    84→```vex
    85→@Cd = @P;
    86→
    87→@Cd = @P;
    88→
    89→@Cd = @P.x;
    90→
    91→@Cd = @N.y;
    92→```
    93→Demonstrates assigning position and normal components to color attributes. When using @P for color, points maintain their color based on world-space position regardless of transforms applied to the geometry. Component access (.x, .y) allows mapping individual vector components to color values, showing how negative positions result in over-dark colors (below black).
    94→
    95→### Position vs Normal Color Assignment [[Ep1, 17:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gB1zBa9Lg4&t=1050s)]
    96→```vex
    97→@Cd = @P;
    98→
    99→@Cd = @P.x;
